summary: Local tonic transport server/client seam for generated backbone write RPCs.
claim_boundary: Local tonic transport seam only. This slice wraps generated messenger, mail, social, and community server traits around the existing generated request-to-write-plan adapters and exposes generated clients over tonic::transport::Channel. A loopback test exercises all implemented write RPC families over 127.0.0.1:0. It does not provide TLS/mTLS, service-gateway admission, production deployment, service discovery, database execution, broker publish, daemon supervision, SLO evidence, or hyperscaler certification.

source_basis.use: Official tonic 0.14.6 transport docs for the server/client transport feature boundary and batteries-included HTTP/2 transport surface.
Official tonic Server docs for builder/add_service/serve_with_incoming_shutdown runtime composition.
Official tonic Endpoint docs for connecting transport Channels used by generated clients.
Official tonic Channel docs for the generated-client channel type used in client factories.

facets.F1_simplicity: One isolated transport adapter crate owns tonic Server/Channel composition; generated bindings stay in the generated adapter, and domain/API/usecase crates remain tonic/prost-free.
facets.F2_hyperscaler: The seam proves generated RPCs can cross a real local TCP tonic server boundary before production gateway, TLS, service discovery, and deployment slices are introduced separately.
facets.F3_adversarial: Tests exercise a real loopback server for messenger, mail, social, community create/vote/moderation plus negative paths for missing generated envelope and vote-before-post state.
facets.F4_api_contract: Generated server trait implementations preserve generated response types and map app/write-plan receipts into proto responses for all implemented write RPC families.
facets.F5_quality: Focused transport-adapter tests plus the 45-package backbone check/test/clippy/fmt matrix, cargo-deny, license-policy, cargo-prefix, catalog/data-class known-blocker probes, parse/config validation, dependency-seam, honest-claims, and diff hygiene are part of this run.
facets.F6_operations: The public serve_backbone_grpc_until_shutdown function composes the six generated service servers over a caller-supplied TcpIncoming and shutdown future; operational supervision remains deliberately out of scope.
facets.F7_security_privacy: The adapter transports only reference IDs and write-plan receipts in tests; no raw message body, mail body, social media blob, credential, broker URL, database URL, or TLS key material is introduced.
facets.F8_supply_chain: No new direct third-party dependency name is introduced; existing tonic/tokio dependency rationales now explicitly allow the isolated transport adapter. Enabling tonic router/transport adds transitive lock entries such as axum 0.8.9, axum-core 0.5.6, hyper-timeout 0.5.2, matchit 0.8.4, try-lock 0.2.5, and want 0.3.1, all covered by cargo-deny license/source checks.
facets.F9_testing: Focused tests passed for 3 transport-adapter unit tests and the broad backbone matrix passed 286 unit tests plus the existing ignored metrics adapter doctest.
facets.F10_ci_cd: GitHub Actions and Jenkins package matrices include the transport adapter in all four service lanes; this does not claim remote CI execution.
facets.F11_observability: Responses carry generated RPC receipt metadata, idempotency keys, policy refs, and audit correlation IDs where the proto response contracts define those fields; future interceptors can bind to the same generated services.
facets.F13_reversibility: The runtime transport seam is isolated to one adapter crate plus workspace/catalog/CI/task/rationale/evidence wiring; reverting it leaves generated bindings and write-plan adapters intact.
